symbols.note: from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 --full; '-' addresses (null) mean the method was not found in bg3_dx11.exe; the component lists come from the method parameter types, not from the code.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Reached through the free function esv::party::LEGACY_AddExperience (EoCServer.dll+0xAC3090), whose callers were not found. It does not touch any component: it adds the amount to a tally kept in the system, indexed by party and by XP type (started at the amount if there is none yet), and logs 'LEGACY AddExperience: party xp type'. Ordinary character XP (esv::Character::AddExperience, used by quest rewards) goes to exp::ExperienceSystem::LEGACY_IncreaseExperience and does not pass here.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, LEGACY_AddExperience at EoCServer.dll+0xACF440: the log string and the two branches that add to or set an int in a per-key array. Review (Opus, 14 Nov): esv::Character::AddExperience at EoCServer.dll+0x15DD760 calls LEGACY_IncreaseExperience, not the party tally.

does.text: Each Update it walks the tally and, for every entry, creates a new entity through the deferred command buffer carrying ExperienceRequestOneFrameComponent (party handle, amount as int, XP type as byte). So one such entity appears per party per XP type in the frame after LEGACY_AddExperience fed the tally. Whether the tally is then cleared was not read.
does.evidence: Review (Opus, 14 Nov): EoCServer.dll+0xAD15E0: CreateEntity then helper +0xAC7E90, an AllocRaw add of DAT_182237644 = ExperienceRequestOneFrameComponent (0x10 bytes), with the three field writes; type resolved in review.

does.text: For each merged-party event entity it logs 'PartyMerged event: source target' and records the party handles in the frame lists so that later steps can carry party data over; what those steps do with the lists was not read.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, ProcessPartyMergedEvents at EoCServer.dll+0xAD1980: query loop, log string, list insert.

does.text: Mirror of the merged handler for split events: logs 'PartySplit event: old new' and records the handles in the second frame list.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, ProcessPartySplitEvents (223 lines): same structure as the merged one.

does.text: Takes recipe requests from story code (LEGACY_UnlockRecipe) and adds a recipe name to the party's recipe list unless it is already there ('already contains recipe').
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, log strings 'Recipe request: party', 'already contains recipe' only.

does.text: Applies queued unlock requests to a party's waypoints component; ProcessWaypointLockRequests does the reverse for lock requests.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, log strings 'UnlockWaypoint request' and 'LockWaypoint request' only.

does.text: Adds a discovered portal to the party's portal list unless it is already listed, and removes portals whose entity is dead ('Found dead portals').
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, log strings only.

does.text: Start of frame: removes the one-frame components this system owns from entities.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll named pseudo-code, one 'Can't remove component' assert and a loop; which types it removes was not resolved.

unknown: What the merge and split handlers do with the party handles they record.
How ProcessUnlockRecipes decides what to unlock (read through log strings only, if at all).
Where the XP tally is emptied besides ProcessExperienceRequests.
Which game action reaches esv::party::LEGACY_AddExperience: no caller found; a story call granting XP to a party is a guess.
sure: no: the XP request path is read to the component and its type (resolved in review), but what calls it is not known; the other handlers come from log strings
